# Independent scientific review of frozen Q52 and Q17

27 October 2026. This review concerns the supplied frozen returns and the original scientific interface. It contains no policy or model ranking.

**Decision.** Q52 supports its general one-step analytic coercive inverse and its smoothed quadratic full-law theorem under the stated Gaussian divergence and regularity hypotheses. Its frozen cosine sampler has a valid exact-real, full-law fixture certificate after paid fitting and analytic verification. Q17 supports the pointwise inverse obstruction, including actual admissible first-order forcings without an L2 inverse, and its capped near-affine positive filling under an additional source promise. Both predictive-family theorems are supported at their stated family and reuse scopes. Neither return completes the general N687 value-query compiler or generic unknown-CP predictive acquisition. No further physical realization or external confirmation is required to accept these mathematical statements at these scopes. Historical novelty and practical advantage were not established by this review.

**Exposure and procedure.** The task itself identified these as native-Pro first returns and supplied the Q52/Q17 labels. Therefore this was not blind to that shared identity. I received no policy mapping or correspondence between the two labels and an orchestration action. Scientific source text mentions historical “Ultra” and “Luna” work, and packet prose mentions a colleague/helper; those are actual incidental exposures. I did not inspect memory, programme chats, dispatchers, Dots, policies/protocols, action/forecast/admission folders, warm continuations, live producers, or other review outputs. No messages, chats, goals, automations, or subagents were created. The only network use was installing SciPy into this owned review directory to run the supplied numerical checks; no external scientific or novelty lookup was performed.

I copied the neutral packets into `owned_Q52` and `owned_Q17`, verified all 27 and 10 manifest entries respectively, and left those copies unchanged. # A coercive Stein correction with a proved smoothed full-law bound

27 October 2026. Independent mathematical audit and extension within this chat.
This is an analytic construction, not an acquired value-query sampler. The
frozen sources are unchanged. No historical novelty claim is made.

The governing opening is S3, sections 16–18 of the frozen packet. That source
has a formal positive Newton identity and an unbounded source-derivative
obstruction for a baseline Gaussian inverse. The construction below uses a
different inverse, allows globally rather than conditionally centered
corrections, and proves an actual one-step smoothed total-variation estimate.

## 1. Setting and conventions

Let Q have standard Gaussian law gamma_n. Rowwise Gaussian divergence is the
closed adjoint of the weak gradient:

    delta v = Q dot v - div v,
    E[delta v f] = E[v dot Df].

Let X: R^n -> R^d be square integrable, with mean mu. Let B be a d by n
matrix field whose rows are in the divergence domain and satisfy

    delta B = X - mu.

Suppose the horizontal derivative matrix

    tau = B (DX)^T

exists weakly, tau is essentially bounded in operator norm, and

    sym tau >= c I_d,             c > 0,
    ||B||op <= M.

Put R = sym tau - I_d and r = ||R||_{L2(gamma_n;Frobenius)}.
All norms on matrix fields below are Frobenius L2 norms unless indicated.

A convenient sufficient regularity class is: B locally C1 and bounded;
X locally Lipschitz, square integrable; tau bounded. The proofs also extend
to a closed horizontal Sobolev calculus with the stated chain and product
rules. No strong derivative of the correction u is assumed or used in the
full-law bound.

## 2. The closed variational inverse

Let H be the space of symmetric matrix fields S in L2 for which
delta(SB) belongs to L2, with its graph norm. Equivalently one may take the
closure of smooth compactly supported symmetric fields and include the
admissible noncompact test fields by localization. Bounded multiplication by
B and closedness of divergence imply closedness of this graph space.

Define

    u_S = delta(SB),
    a(S,T) = E[u_S dot u_T] + E[<S tau,T>_F].

The form is generally nonsymmetric. It is nevertheless continuous and
coercive:

    a(S,S) = ||u_S||_2^2 + E tr(S^2 sym tau)
           >= ||u_S||_2^2 + c ||S||_2^2.

Lax–Milgram therefore gives a unique S in H satisfying

    a(S,T) = -E[<R,T>_F]

# Scalar all-order correction: domain audit

27 October 2026. This audits the scalar construction developed by the
gaussian_challenge colleague within the same chat. It is not a value-only
implementation or a historical novelty assertion.

Let gamma be the underlying finite-dimensional Gaussian measure. Let
V=B dot D be a closable derivation with the chain/product rules on a dense
core, B bounded, and Gaussian adjoint

    V* = m - V,       m=X-mu,       Vm=tau.

Suppose m is in L2 and tau is bounded with

    tau=1+R,       ||R||infinity=rho<1.

These conditions hold initially for the scalar source construction
X=h(G)+Z, B=(K(G),1), with bounded weak h', bounded C1 K, and ell<1.
The same conclusions may be obtained first for smooth tame fields and
then by the horizontal energy closure described below.

## 1. The useful form identity

For bounded core S, integration by parts applied to V(m S^2) gives

    E m^2 S^2 = E tau S^2 + 2 E[m S VS].

Consequently

    ||V*S||_2^2 = ||VS||_2^2 + E tau S^2.      (1)

The scalar coercive inverse therefore has the symmetric Dirichlet form

    E[VS VT] + 2 E[tau ST] = -E[RT].         (2)

This is more useful than asserting a Feynman–Kac diffusion without proving
that the degenerate diffusion is complete. Equation (2), on the closed
horizontal Sobolev space, suffices.

## 2. The maximum principle uses truncation tests

Set c=1-rho and A=rho/(2c). Use T=(S-A)_+ in (2), by the Markov chain rule
for the closed derivative. On {S>A}, 2 tau S >= 2cA=rho. Since -R<=rho,

    E[1_{S>A}|VS|^2] + 2c E[(S-A)_+^2] <= 0.

Thus S<=A. The negative-part test gives S>=-A, so

    ||S||infinity <= rho/[2(1-rho)].           (3)

Identity (1) and bounded S imply u=V*S=mS-VS is in L2. This also shows
that the solution of the Dirichlet problem belongs to the divergence
graph space used by the matrix construction. In a complete proof,
truncation/localization justifies (1) for this weak solution; the factors
m,VS are L2 and S,tau are bounded, so all displayed products are integrable.

## 3. Exact weak residual update

Equation (2) is equivalently

    Vu + S tau = -R,
    u=V*S.

Put

    X+=X+u,        B+=(1+S)B,        V+=(1+S)V.

Divergence gives delta B+=X+-mu, hence the mean is unchanged. Horizontal
chain/product rules give

    tau+=V+X+=(1+S)(tau+Vu),
    tau+-1 = -S R - S^2 tau.                   (4)

This is a pointwise-a.e./horizontal
